assignments.title: Wire the existing FR-013 conflict-detection sweep into the real Zone 3 and Zone 5 write paths

invest.independent: Both collaborators this story wires together already exist and are independently tested: ConflictDetectingProvenanceRepository (src/dashanan/application/conflict_detection_sweep.py) and SqlSemanticRepository/EntityMemoryRepository (src/dashanan/infrastructure/sql_semantic_repository.py, entity_memory_repository.py). This story only needs both to already exist, not any new Sprint 3 work first.
invest.negotiable: Does not reopen HLD Section 3.8's conflict-detection algorithm (the `(entity, predicate)`/`(subject, predicate, object)` contradiction check, the `-0.3` disputed-confidence modifier) - that mechanism is locked and already implemented; only the write-path CALL SITE is in scope.
invest.valuable: Closes a real, source-verified gap: this session confirmed by grep that ConflictDetectingProvenanceRepository and composition_root.py's build_provenance_repository are imported ONLY by each other and by test files - SqlSemanticRepository and EntityMemoryRepository never import or call either. SRS.md's FR-013 row ('this is required scope, not optional, since Zone 3/5 writes cannot satisfy NFR-011 without it') is currently unmet at the integration point despite the underlying mechanism being real and tested.
invest.estimable: 5 story points: composition-root-style dependency injection wiring two existing write paths through an existing decorator - comparable in shape to DASH-STORY-012..020's Sprint 2 adapter/composition-root wiring work, not a new-mechanism build.
invest.small: Scoped to the two call sites (Zone 3's write path in SqlSemanticRepository, Zone 5's write_attribute in EntityMemoryRepository) routing through ConflictDetectingProvenanceRepository/detect_conflict - it does not touch Zone 4 (excluded per FR-013's own text, which names only Zone 3 and Zone 5) or any other zone's write path.
invest.testable: Concrete and behavioral: seed a contradicting write for the same (entity, predicate) or (subject, predicate, object) through the real Zone 3/Zone 5 write path (not directly against ConflictDetectingProvenanceRepository, as the existing unit tests already do) and confirm both records land as conflict_status=disputed with reduced confidence, per SRS.md AC-015.

assignments.gap_confirmed: CONFIRMED by direct source-code read in this session (not assumed from DSHN-53's empty Jira description). assignments.title: DPDP erasure-cascade reach into Zone 3 (Semantic) and Zone 5 (Entity) data
assignments.traces_to_fr: NFR-006 / AC-013 (no new FR minted - see fr_minting_decision below)

invest.independent: Builds on SubjectErasureCascadeService (DASH-STORY-020, Sprint 2, already landed) and CrossZoneDpdpErasureCascade (DSHN-58, already landed) without requiring either to change - this story adds new Zone 3/Zone 5 erasure legs and, per DSHN-70's own recommendation, a single orchestrator that fans both existing services plus the two new legs out from one subject-erasure request.
invest.negotiable: Does not reopen AC-013's crypto-shredding erasure mechanism itself (a separate, already-disclosed gap per SRS.md Section 4.1's own AC-013 Implementation Scope Note) - this story closes the ZONE-REACH gap (which zones the cascade touches), not the MECHANISM gap (crypto-shredding vs. plain delete/eviction).
invest.valuable: Closes a real, test-verified gap. tests/integration/test_cross_zone_dpdp_erasure_scope_gap.py (read in full this session) proves with real seeded data and a real erasure-cascade call that Zone 3 (SemanticEdge) and Zone 5 (EntityRecord attribute) data for an erased subject_id survives SubjectErasureCascadeService.request_erasure completely untouched, while the job still reports COMPLETED - 'the behavior that makes the Zone 3/5 no-op... easy to miss: the 202/job-completion contract looks identical whether or not Zone 3/4/5 were actually reached' (that test file's own module docstring).
invest.estimable: 5 story points: two new erasure legs (Zone 3 by subject_ref, Zone 5 by entity_id) plus a single fan-out orchestrator wiring them alongside the two already-existing cascades - comparable in shape to DASH-STORY-020's original Zone 8 erasure-cascade story (also 5 SP).
invest.small: Scoped to exactly the two zones DSHN-70's own text and this session's own verification confirm are reachable: Zone 3 (SemanticEdge.subject_ref) and Zone 5 (EntityRecord attributes keyed by entity_id). Zone 4 (Procedure) is explicitly and correctly excluded, not silently dropped - see zone_4_exclusion below.
invest.testable: Concrete: the same tests/integration/test_cross_zone_dpdp_erasure_scope_gap.py assertions this story is built to fix (currently asserting the NO-OP) are updated to assert the OPPOSITE - Zone 3/Zone 5 data for an erased subject_id no longer survives a real request_erasure call - which is the cleanest possible acceptance signal since the gap-documenting test already exists.

assignments.gap_confirmed: CONFIRMED by direct read of tests/integration/test_cross_zone_dpdp_erasure_scope_gap.py in this session. Its three tests demonstrate: (1) a real SemanticEdge seeded for a subject_id survives request_erasure with zero additional SQL statements issued against Zone 3's connection; (2) a real Zone 5 EntityRecord attribute for the same subject_id survives request_erasure, confirmed by a direct read-after-erasure (not just an executed-statement proxy); (3) the erasure job itself still completes successfully and reports COMPLETED with item_ids == () even though Zones 3/5 were never touched - the module docstring's own words: 'the 202/job-completion contract looks identical whether or not Zone 3/4/5 were actually reached.'
assignments.zone_4_exclusion: Zone 4 (Procedure, HLD Section 3.5) is a documented, correct EXCLUSION carried forward from the test file's own docstring, not an oversight this story needs to fix: Procedure's real, current field set (tenant_id, task_signature_hash, steps, success_count, failure_count, last_used_at, state, score_terms) carries no subject_id, entity_id, or any other subject-linkable reference at all (per dashanan.domain.procedure.Procedure's own docstring, which the test file cites). There is no real DPDP erasure leg to build for Zone 4 without first adding a subject-linkable field to the Procedure domain model itself, which is out of this story's scope.
